items.body: Every case in scope passed. No Failed or Inconclusive result stands, so no defect record is owed for this run.

With the owning organisation's Auto Reissue checkbox off, the Reissue button was correctly hidden and Manual Reissue was missing too — Void / Cancel appeared in its place, while the page's own API reported canManualReissue: true. Manual Reissue appeared only on the one booking held by a different user. Seen four times across both modules.

sections.title: Requirement Coverage
blocks: Computed from the Traceability Matrix of both modules. 7 of 7 testable requirement rows verified, 1 open question, 0 partially verified, 0 uncovered.

items: PO-28 — the button needs the checkbox AND a matching credential (supersedes PO-22): VERIFIED by TC-AGENCY-082 and TC-BR-103 in the negative, and by TC-AGENCY-076, 079, 081, TC-BR-101, 104 in the positive.
PO-16 — Agency and Branch checkboxes are independent: VERIFIED (TC-AGENCY-078, TC-BR-104).
PO-24 — the Itinerary condition is Status Booked: VERIFIED (TC-AGENCY-084, 094, TC-BR-112).
PO-25 — the Portal is in scope and shows Reissue without a lock: VERIFIED (TC-AGENCY-079, 080, 081, 094).
PO-26 — an on-behalf booking follows the Agency it belongs to: VERIFIED (TC-AGENCY-083).
spec §5 — the Itinerary's display conditions: VERIFIED for the Reissue button on all four covering cases. The Manual Reissue half is out of scope (PO-29) and deliberately not verified.
RSK-013 — which value the Itinerary uses while a change is pending: NOT VERIFIED, open question. The behaviour was recorded, not judged.
PO-29 — Manual Reissue is out of scope for this story: a scope decision, asserted by no case.
PO-22 — the button is independent of the selected credential: WITHDRAWN on 2026-09-27, replaced by PO-28.

The run was headless. This stage normally runs with a visible browser so a person can watch each step. The user was asked beforehand and chose headless. Screenshots and API responses were captured as usual, so no result changes — what is missing is the live human observation.

A scope decision was taken mid-stage. Three approved cases asserted something about Manual Reissue when this run began. The product owner ruled it out of scope (PO-29) afterwards and the clause was removed. Two cases changed from Failed to Passed because the expectation changed, not because anything was re-run.

Credential 313 had to be borrowed. Both organisations had been reduced to a single credential after run-006, so the wrong-credential state did not exist. NDCsbr / 313 was attached with the user's explicit go-ahead, used, and detached again.
One lock was left in place — NDCEG-BR-F2609242aZ6EJ was already held by odeysysadmin before this run began.
The test design was amended and approved the same day, by the person who requested the change. A reviewer wanting an independent check should read modules/*/test_design/ first.
Video and console logs were not collected. Screenshots, API responses and structured per-case observations were.
REC-008-1 — Pass the Manual Reissue observation to whoever owns the Itinerary action bar, as information rather than as a defect of this story.
REC-008-2 — Answer the question run-006 raised as REC-1: should the Itinerary act on an Auto Reissue change nobody has approved yet? Today it does.
REC-008-3 — Record PO-28 as confirmed in the reissue-flow context and close run-007's DS-2.
REC-008-4 — Keep a second reissue-eligible credential permanently attached to AGN9780 and BRN265, so TC-AGENCY-082 and TC-BR-103 can run without changing Product Access each time.
REC-008-5 — Re-check the remaining 48 auto-reissue cases from run-006 against PO-28; this run covered only the button-display ones.
